title: TypeScript final assessment question set

questions.prompt: Final assessment: What is the purpose of a precise TypeScript type?
options: To convert or sanitize an external value at runtime.
To make every property immutable.
To replace all application tests.
To express the intended values and let the compiler detect incompatible uses.
questions.answer_key: To express the intended values and let the compiler detect incompatible uses.
questions.explanation: Types describe expected program values but do not automatically change or validate runtime data.

questions.prompt: Final assessment: A value has type unknown. What is the safe next step before using it as a string?
options: Cast it to string without checking its value.
Use it directly because unknown disables type checks.
Convert the variable to any and assume the data is valid.
Check its runtime type or validate its shape, then narrow it before using string-only operations.
questions.answer_key: Check its runtime type or validate its shape, then narrow it before using string-only operations.
questions.explanation: unknown requires evidence before operations that depend on a more specific type.

questions.prompt: Final assessment: What does a TypeScript type assertion do?
options: It changes the JavaScript value into a different object.
It guarantees the asserted type is correct.
It tells the compiler to treat an expression as a type; it does not validate the value at runtime.
It inserts a runtime validator for every field.
questions.answer_key: It tells the compiler to treat an expression as a type; it does not validate the value at runtime.
questions.explanation: Use an assertion only when independent evidence justifies it; validation is separate.

questions.prompt: Final assessment: What is a key benefit of the satisfies operator?
options: It checks compatibility with a target type while preserving useful inference for the expression.
It converts the value into a new runtime object.
It disables all excess-property checks.
It validates API data while the app is running.
questions.answer_key: It checks compatibility with a target type while preserving useful inference for the expression.
questions.explanation: satisfies checks a compile-time contract without simply replacing the expression type with the target annotation.

questions.prompt: Final assessment: How should code safely use a value whose type is a union?
options: Assume the first union member is always present.
Narrow the value using a condition or a discriminator before using member-specific fields.
Access every possible field without checking.
Replace the union with any.
questions.answer_key: Narrow the value using a condition or a discriminator before using member-specific fields.
questions.explanation: Narrowing establishes which union member applies along a control-flow path.

questions.prompt: Final assessment: What is the safest way to use a type or build feature?
options: Assume compiler configuration has identical behavior in every version.
Use any whenever the types become difficult.
Treat type-level examples as proof of runtime correctness.
Choose the feature that expresses the contract, check compiler diagnostics, and verify the configured tool/runtime behavior.
questions.answer_key: Choose the feature that expresses the contract, check compiler diagnostics, and verify the configured tool/runtime behavior.
questions.explanation: Type and build features must be evaluated in the actual configured project.

questions.prompt: Final assessment: When is a tuple more suitable than a general array?
options: When the values must be fetched from a database.
When runtime validation should be skipped.
When positions have known types and ordering, such as a [string, number] pair.
When all elements must be unrelated values with no positional meaning.
questions.answer_key: When positions have known types and ordering, such as a [string, number] pair.
questions.explanation: Tuples express a known sequence of positions and types.

questions.prompt: Final assessment: What is Record<Key, Value> most useful for?
options: Guaranteeing that external input has been validated.
Describing an object mapping a set of keys to values of a consistent type.
Executing SQL queries.
Changing a type into a database table at runtime.
questions.answer_key: Describing an object mapping a set of keys to values of a consistent type.
questions.explanation: Record creates a mapped object type; runtime contents still depend on the data and checks.

questions.prompt: Final assessment: What makes a function type useful?
options: It replaces all runtime error handling.
It documents parameter and return contracts so callers and implementations can be checked consistently.
It automatically tests the function at runtime.
It causes the function to run when the type is declared.
questions.answer_key: It documents parameter and return contracts so callers and implementations can be checked consistently.
questions.explanation: Function types are compile-time contracts and should be paired with behavior tests.

questions.prompt: Final assessment: Why define overload signatures?
options: To create multiple runtime implementations with the same function name.
To bypass argument checking.
To guarantee all arguments are valid network data.
To describe multiple supported call shapes with corresponding return types while implementing the behavior once.
questions.answer_key: To describe multiple supported call shapes with corresponding return types while implementing the behavior once.
questions.explanation: Overloads communicate supported call patterns to callers; implementation logic still needs testing.

questions.prompt: Final assessment: What does type narrowing do?
options: It changes the runtime value into another object.
It disables strict checking in the branch.
It proves that every field from JSON is trustworthy.
It refines the possible type of a value within a control-flow branch based on checks.
questions.answer_key: It refines the possible type of a value within a control-flow branch based on checks.
questions.explanation: Narrowing relies on control-flow evidence such as typeof checks, discriminants and user-defined guards.

questions.prompt: Final assessment: How can never help with exhaustive union handling?
options: Assign the remaining value to never so a newly added union member causes a type error.
Use never as the default value for every variable.
It automatically adds missing switch cases at runtime.
It disables diagnostics for the switch.
questions.answer_key: Assign the remaining value to never so a newly added union member causes a type error.
questions.explanation: An exhaustive check makes incomplete handling easier to detect when a union changes.

questions.prompt: Final assessment: How does TypeScript commonly decide whether object types are compatible?
options: Compatibility is decided by checking the database schema at runtime.
Structural compatibility: the value must provide the required members with compatible types.
Only the interface and class names are compared.
Objects are compatible only if constructed by the same factory.
questions.answer_key: Structural compatibility: the value must provide the required members with compatible types.
questions.explanation: TypeScript is largely structurally typed; specialized patterns such as branding add explicit distinctions.

questions.prompt: Final assessment: What is a central advantage of generics?
options: They preserve a relationship between input types and output types without defaulting to any.
They guarantee every runtime input is valid.
They only work for string values.
They remove the need for tests.
questions.answer_key: They preserve a relationship between input types and output types without defaulting to any.
questions.explanation: A well-designed generic preserves useful type information and constrains operations appropriately.

questions.prompt: Final assessment: What does a conditional type do?
options: It creates a database transaction.
It runs only after JavaScript has started.
It selects a type result based on an assignability relationship between types.
It chooses a runtime branch after reading user input.
questions.answer_key: It selects a type result based on an assignability relationship between types.
questions.explanation: Conditional types operate in TypeScript’s type system, not as emitted runtime conditionals.

questions.prompt: Final assessment: What is the purpose of a mapped type?
options: To loop over object properties at runtime.
To map a URL to a server without configuration.
To convert TypeScript to a database schema automatically.
To transform properties by iterating over keys of an existing type.
questions.answer_key: To transform properties by iterating over keys of an existing type.
questions.explanation: Mapped types derive related type shapes and can modify property names or modifiers.

questions.prompt: Final assessment: What should a robust asynchronous API wrapper do?
options: Trust response.json() because its result is automatically verified by TypeScript.
Ignore rejected promises.
Treat a declared response type as a server-side authorization check.
Model success and failure, check response status, and validate decoded data before treating it as a domain object.
questions.answer_key: Model success and failure, check response status, and validate decoded data before treating it as a domain object.
questions.explanation: The type checker does not validate remote data; asynchronous operations can fail independently.

questions.prompt: Final assessment: Which statement correctly distinguishes TypeScript access modifiers and JavaScript private fields?
options: JavaScript #private fields are comments removed before execution.
TypeScript private is primarily a type-checking restriction; JavaScript #private fields enforce runtime privacy.
Both mechanisms are identical in all runtime behavior.
TypeScript private automatically encrypts fields.
questions.answer_key: TypeScript private is primarily a type-checking restriction; JavaScript #private fields enforce runtime privacy.
questions.explanation: Runtime behavior matters when selecting an encapsulation mechanism.

questions.prompt: Final assessment: What must be true for a TypeScript import to work in an application?
options: Type-only imports create runtime values automatically.
The source module specifier, compiler resolution, package exports and actual runtime/bundler must agree.
The compiler always rewrites every alias into a working runtime path.
Any filename extension works with every runtime.
questions.answer_key: The source module specifier, compiler resolution, package exports and actual runtime/bundler must agree.
questions.explanation: Type checking and runtime module loading are related but distinct responsibilities.

questions.prompt: Final assessment: What is the safest way to choose TypeScript compiler settings?
options: Assume every option works in every TypeScript version.
Disable all strict options before inspecting diagnostics.
Align the configuration with the installed compiler, target runtime, libraries and bundler, then type-check the project.
Copy a tsconfig from another project without checking its runtime.
questions.answer_key: Align the configuration with the installed compiler, target runtime, libraries and bundler, then type-check the project.
questions.explanation: Compiler settings describe environment assumptions and change across versions; validate migration and build behavior.

questions.prompt: Final assessment: What should a reliable TypeScript integration do with external data?
options: Treat JSON.parse as a validation step.
Validate data and failures at runtime, while using types to make trusted application contracts explicit.
Assume the declared type validates the server response.
Ignore promise rejections and malformed data.
questions.answer_key: Validate data and failures at runtime, while using types to make trusted application contracts explicit.
questions.explanation: Types and runtime validation solve different problems at external boundaries.

questions.prompt: Final assessment: What should a robust asynchronous API wrapper do?
options: Model success and failure, check response status, and validate decoded data before treating it as a domain object.
Trust response.json() because its result is automatically verified by TypeScript.
Ignore rejected promises.
Treat a declared response type as a server-side authorization check.
questions.answer_key: Model success and failure, check response status, and validate decoded data before treating it as a domain object.
questions.explanation: The type checker does not validate remote data; asynchronous operations can fail independently.

questions.prompt: Final assessment: What should happen at an external trust boundary?
options: Treat incoming data as unknown, validate its structure and policy, then create a trusted domain value.
Cast it to the desired interface and skip validation.
Trust client-submitted roles and ownership fields.
Return secrets in logs to simplify debugging.
questions.answer_key: Treat incoming data as unknown, validate its structure and policy, then create a trusted domain value.
questions.explanation: Compile-time types do not validate external values or enforce authorization by themselves.

questions.prompt: Final assessment: Which test strategy provides stronger evidence than a single passing happy-path example?
options: Test expected behavior, edge cases and failure paths, and add type-level tests for public type contracts where useful.
Only measure line coverage and assume that proves correctness.
Skip tests because code type-checks.
Mock every component so no integration is ever checked.
questions.answer_key: Test expected behavior, edge cases and failure paths, and add type-level tests for public type contracts where useful.
questions.explanation: Coverage is a signal, not proof; test quality depends on assertions, cases and realistic boundaries.

questions.prompt: Final assessment: What is the purpose of a declaration file?
options: It automatically executes package code.
It describes the types of existing JavaScript APIs without providing their runtime implementation.
It replaces the runtime JavaScript implementation.
It proves a package is secure.
questions.answer_key: It describes the types of existing JavaScript APIs without providing their runtime implementation.
questions.explanation: Declaration files describe APIs and should be tested against real consumers and supported versions.

questions.prompt: Final assessment: What is the strongest evidence that an application design is ready for review?
options: Only a screenshot of the happy path.
A successful compile with no runtime checks or acceptance criteria.
Clear domain contracts, implemented behavior, tests for normal and failure cases, and reproducible setup/documentation.
A large number of abstractions without tests.
questions.answer_key: Clear domain contracts, implemented behavior, tests for normal and failure cases, and reproducible setup/documentation.
questions.explanation: Production-oriented work is supported by explicit acceptance criteria and repeatable evidence.

questions.prompt: Final assessment: What should a typed frontend still validate?
options: User input and server responses at runtime, while keeping loading, success and failure states explicit.
Nothing: JSX and TypeScript guarantee every browser value is valid.
The frontend can decide server authorization by itself.
Only CSS class names need types.
questions.answer_key: User input and server responses at runtime, while keeping loading, success and failure states explicit.
questions.explanation: Typed UI models improve development feedback but do not replace runtime validation or server-side checks.

questions.prompt: Final assessment: What is a reliable compiler-version migration approach?
options: Assume old compiler options and tooling always remain supported.

Upgrade in a branch, review deprecation diagnostics, test dependencies and builds, then roll out with a rollback plan.
Change the version directly in production and ignore warnings.
